Context: This update looks at Ethnic Wear revenue in May vs. April. Any month-on-month change above 8.0% in either direction is reviewed.
Insight: [Fact] Ethnic Wear revenue rose from INR 104,520.77 in April to INR 185,107.61 in May, a change of 77.1%. [Fact] Orders went from 64 to 104 over the same period.
Implication: [Hypothesis] The rise may reflect a May-specific demand driver, such as a promotion or seasonal push, because orders and revenue moved together; the figures alone do not show why. [Action] Ask the regional leads whether any Ethnic Wear promotion or seasonal stocking ran in May; if none did, find another explanation before May is used as a planning baseline. [Action] Split May's INR 185,107.61 by order status (delivered, returned, cancelled, pending); if delivered revenue is much lower, treat the 77.1% change as overstated.

Context: This update looks at Western Wear revenue in May vs. April. Any month-on-month change above 8.0% in either direction is reviewed.
Insight: [Fact] Western Wear revenue fell from INR 113,866.15 in April to INR 86,998.18 in May, a change of -23.6%. [Fact] Orders went from 79 to 64 over the same period.
Implication: [Hypothesis] The fall may be the April demand driver ending, rather than a new weakness, because orders and revenue moved together; the figures alone do not show why. [Action] Ask the regional leads whether the April Western Wear promotion or seasonal demand ended, and whether any May stock shortage held back Western Wear orders. [Action] Compare May's Western Wear orders with April's region by region: a drop concentrated in one region points to a local problem to fix, while an even drop points to a change in demand.
